title: LabeledClause
description: A single labeled clause chunk. This is the shared data contract flowing through the segmenter, synthetic data generation, model fine-tuning, and the risk engine. Every stage of the ML pipeline reads or writes objects in this shape.

text.description: The clause text exactly as it appears in the (segmented) document, in its original language.

language.description: BCP-47-style short code for the clause's language. Extend this enum if a third language (e.g. Malvi) is added later.

doc_type.description: Which of the 3 supported MVP document types this clause came from.

clause_category.description: Exactly one of the 13 taxonomy tags. Single-label by design (matches roadmap's 'Sequence Classification' framing) - do not add multi-label support without revisiting the fine-tuning approach.

risk_label.description: Soft risk signal for this specific clause instance, independent of its category. 'not_applicable' is for categories where risk genuinely doesn't apply in context (e.g. a plain duration statement with nothing unusual).

related_provision_ids.description: Optional links to provision_id values in the legal-corpus JSON files (e.g. 'bonded-labour-1976-core-prohibition'). Populated when a clause is a training example for a specific known risk pattern. This field seeds the RAG explanation step's citation trail.

source.description: Provenance tag. REQUIRED and must be honest - this is how you track how much of your training data is real vs. bootstrap vs. synthetic, which matters for evaluating model reliability later.
